description: Canonical ObservationType namespace. Observation.ObservationType (src/DumpDetective.Sdk/Observations/Observation.cs) is a free-form string, not an enum, by design (docs/refactor/modularity/observation-and-correlation-model.md § 7 keeps it open until enough producers exist to justify closing it) — this registry is the checked-in record of every type actually emitted today, so a typo or a silent rename is a diffable, reviewable event instead of an invisible string drift. Cross-checked against real analyzer output by tests/DumpDetective.Tests/Unit/Architecture/SdkRegistryConformanceTests.cs. Purity rules for every entry's measures (raw only, never a severity/weighted composite) are in Observation.cs's own remarks and observation-and-correlation-model.md § 2a.

contention.episode.note: Named 'contention.episode', not the earlier design table's 'contention.hotspot' — 'hotspot' is a ranking/severity claim, which observation purity rules push to a synthesis rule (Phase 5, not yet built) instead. See the analyzer's own remarks.

cpu.sample-attribution.note: Named 'cpu.sample-attribution', not 'cpu.hotspot', same reasoning as contention.episode above. Leaf-frame-only (exclusive samples), not an inclusive call-tree breakdown — see the analyzer's own remarks.

heap.root.note: Phase 5 step 1's pilot analyzer (docs/refactor/modularity/phase-5-observations-synthesis.md). One observation per RootFinding — no root-kind measure here; see root.kind-summary for per-kind breakdowns.

root.kind-summary.note: One per GCRootDomainResult.ByKind row — bounded to HeapRootKind's fixed, small taxonomy (Stack, StaticVar, FinalizerQueue, StrongHandle, PinnedHandle, ...), not per-root. Same kind.ordinal-measure pattern as heap.loh-fragmentation/heap.segment-kind-composition. Backs the old finding generator's static-root/finalizer-queue/pinned-handle signals, which heap.root (no root-kind measure) cannot.

root.population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. TotalRoots includes roots dropped before ByKind/heap.root ever see them (null target, unresolvable metadata, zero-size object), so it cannot be reconstructed by summing root.kind-summary's own count measure.

handle.pinned.note: One observation per already-bounded GCHandleDomainResult.TopPinnedHandleAddresses entry, not per handle.

handle.population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Backs every old finding-generator signal handle.pinned cannot (it is capped to TopPinnedHandleAddressesToShow, not the whole population). Also carries GCHandleAnalysisOptions' warning thresholds as measures rather than hard-coding defaults into the synthesis rule — unlike other analyzers' fixed generator constants, these are genuinely runtime-configurable via AnalysisContext.AnalyzerOptions.

handle.refcounted-target.note: One per distinct RefCounted (COM interop RCW) handle target type — bounded by distinct type count, not per-handle. Backs the old finding generator's dominant-type narrative text, which handle.pinned (Pinned/AsyncPinned only) cannot.

finalizer.queue-entry.note: One observation per valid finalizer-queue entry (the whole queue, uncapped by design — see the analyzer's own remarks). shallow.bytes and is-critical-finalizer added Phase 5 step 2 to back the old finding generator's CriticalFinalizerObject signal, which read entry.ShallowSize/IsCriticalFinalizerType.

type.finalizable-population.note: One per finalizable type from heap.types' per-type aggregates (§21.1 population sweep) — every finalizable type, not capped. Backs the old finding generator's Gen2 accumulation signal (total count/bytes, top type by Gen2 count), which finalizer.queue-entry (queue population only) cannot.

finalizer.queue-population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Carries the full finalizer-queue count including invalid ("<unknown>"-typed) entries, which finalizer.queue-entry never observes individually since they have no resolvable Type for a Subject.

weakhandle.target.note: One observation per alive weak-handle target (Phase A). retained.bytes is omitted, not zeroed, when no dominator tree is available. held-only-via-weak-reference added Phase 5 step 2 — 1.0 when the target is unreachable from any GC root (the weak handle is its only known reference), 0.0 otherwise; always 0.0, never 1.0, when reachability wasn't computed at all (see weakreference.population's held-only-detection-available).

weakreference.stale-wrapper.note: One observation per WeakReference<T> instance whose m_handle field reads 0 (Phase B) — only the stale subset, not every WeakReference<T> instance.

weakreference.population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Dead weak handles never get a weakhandle.target observation at all (nothing to point Subjects at once the target is collected), and WeakReferenceObjectCount/Bytes cover every WeakReference<T> instance, not just the stale subset weakreference.stale-wrapper observes — neither is reconstructable by counting/summing the per-target observations.

gc.generation-composition.note: Single whole-heap observation per run — the canonical gc.generation-composition example named in observation-and-correlation-model.md § 2a. No entity subject (whole-process scalar). Per-type breakdown deliberately deferred (unbounded volume risk) — see gc.generation-top-allocator/gc.generation-top-accumulator for the bounded exception Phase 5 step 2 carved out. loh.percent/gen2.percent are genuinely distinct from loh.fraction/gen2.fraction despite the similar names: the *.fraction measures are byte-fraction-of-total-managed-bytes (computed here at emission time), loh.percent is GCGenerationDomainResult.LohPercent (a byte-based percentage with a POH-excluding denominator) and gen2.percent is Gen2Pct (count-based, objects not bytes) — both are what GCGenerationFindingGenerator actually reads. FallbackMode/GenBytesAreApproximate need no measures of their own: they're already Provenance.Fidelity/Observation.Confidence above. The three *-pressure.threshold measures carry GCGenerationAnalysisOptions' runtime-configurable defaults rather than the synthesis rule hard-coding them, same choice GCHandleSynthesisRule made.

gc.generation-top-allocator.note: Up to 3 types, selected and ranked by the analyzer itself (SelectTopTypes, ported from the old finding generator's BuildTopTypeEvidence) from the full, not-observed PerTypeGenerationProfiles population — framework-namespace types (System.*/Microsoft.*/...) deprioritized behind application types the same way the old generator's evidence text did. Doing the selection analyzer-side, not in the synthesis rule, is what keeps this bounded to ≤3 instead of the full per-type population's volume risk.

gc.generation-top-accumulator.note: Up to 3 types, ranked by exact Gen2 bytes when any type in the full population has them (gc.generation-composition's has-gen2-bytes), otherwise by Gen2 instance count — same selection/fallback gc.generation-composition's own note describes for gc.generation-top-allocator. Both gen2.bytes and gen2.count are always carried so the synthesis rule can pick the right text format per has-gen2-bytes without a second observation type.

gc.allocation-composition.note: Count-based whole-heap composition, distinct from GCGenerationAnalyzer's byte-based gc.generation-composition — independent corroborating measurement, not duplication (observation-and-correlation-model.md § 4). Excludes AllocationProfile and the four Top*Types lists (Smell B — bucketed by a hand-picked threshold, not a raw fact) as classifications, but Phase 5 step 2 added the *raw* size-fraction measures (gen0/gen2/loh) the pressure/profile classifiers need, plus transient-classification.threshold — AllocationPatternAnalysisOptions.TransientClassificationThreshold is runtime-configurable, so the synthesis rule reads it here rather than hard-coding the 70.0 default, same choice GCHandleSynthesisRule made for its own thresholds. gen1.size-fraction is deliberately not added: no finding reads it. An EvidenceRef with the single top-by-composite-score long-lived type's name as its Description is present only when TopLongLivedTypes is non-empty — that unbounded, composite-ranked list itself is not observed per-entry (the same volume risk this note's own Smell-B exclusion already flags), only the one identity the old finding generator actually reads.

heap.segment-composition.note: One observation per generation label (bounded to at most 6). No segment entity kind exists yet, so generation.ordinal carries which row this is, same convention as gc.suspend-reason.

heap.memory-composition.note: Single whole-heap observation per run — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Backs MemoryFindingGenerator's pressure-score/concentration/small-object/LOH findings; MemoryPressureClassifier itself (internal to a different assembly) is not called, its formula is duplicated in MemorySynthesisRule, same choice AllocationPatternSynthesisRule made. top1-type.bytes and the top-1 type's name (as EvidenceRef.Description) are present only when TopTypes is non-empty — TopTypes itself is the full, unbounded per-type population (same volume risk GCGenerationAnalyzer's own PerTypeGenerationProfiles note flags) and is not observed per-entry; only the single top-1 identity the finding generator actually reads is. Top10BytesPercent is deliberately not carried: no finding reads it.

heap.loh-fragmentation.note: One observation per LOH/POH kind breakdown row (bounded to at most 2: Large, Pinned).

heap.loh-type-composition.note: One observation per type that actually has LOH objects — bounded to a small fraction of the whole-heap type population, unlike GCGenerationAnalyzer's per-type list.

heap.segment-reservation.note: Single whole-heap observation per run. Excludes AddressSpacePressureRisk/PressureRiskReason — a hand-picked-threshold classification (Smell A); SegmentReservationSynthesisRule (Phase 5 step 2) re-derives both from dump-pointer-size/reserved.bytes/reserved-to-committed.ratio and the three threshold measures below, the same re-derive-don't-store choice AllocationPatternSynthesisRule made for AllocationProfile. The three threshold measures and dump-pointer-size/logical-heap.count are genuinely raw config/facts, not judgment, so they were safe to add directly. NearEmptyRegionCount/NearEmptyRegionCommittedBytes need no measures here: when IsRegionsBased, they're exact sums over heap.region-composition's own near-empty.count/near-empty.committed-bytes (already emitted for every region-generation bucket, not a capped sample); IsRegionsBased itself is reconstructed as "did any heap.region-composition arrive".

heap.region-composition.note: One observation per region-generation bucket (bounded to at most 7), only emitted when the dump is regions-based (.NET 9+ GC).

thread.blocked.note: One per deadlock-candidate thread (alive, holds a lock, blocked on a monitor). Named for the canonical example in observation-and-correlation-model.md § 4 — 'deadlock' is a synthesis-rule judgment, not this raw fact.

lock.contested.note: One per contested lock. Subjects carries the lock's type, plus the owning thread as a second subject when resolved (a relation, per observation-and-correlation-model.md § 1's Subjects remarks).

thread.wait-state.note: One per alive thread that is actually waiting — a proper subset of all alive threads. WaitType/WaitReason omitted (categorical, no enum instance left in scope by the time the domain result exists); circular-wait-candidate.count is the raw per-thread fact (MonitorWait + holding a lock) HangHealthClassifier's deadlock-candidate penalty needs.

runtime.hang-pressure.note: Whole-run — thread-pool saturation/backpressure counters have no natural per-entity subject, same shape as gc.generation-composition.

thread.state.note: One per alive thread — bounded by real thread count, never heap-scale.

thread.stack-cluster.note: One per distinct call-stack-shape cluster among alive threads (filtered by MinClusterSize). No entity subject — a cluster spans many threads; SampleOsThreadIds is a sample, not full membership.

infra.sql-connection-pool.note: One per discovered ADO.NET connection-pool manager instance — a handful per process, never heap-scale. max.size/min.size omitted when unresolved.

infra.sql-command.note: One per active command instance — only the active subset, not every scanned candidate.

infra.sql-command-population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Covers every scanned candidate, including disposed and unreadable-state ones infra.sql-command never observes individually (only active commands get one) — ActiveCount itself is reconstructable by counting those, so it isn't duplicated here.

infra.sql-transaction.note: One per active transaction instance — only the active subset.

infra.sql-transaction-population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Covers every scanned candidate, including disposed and unresolvable-state ones infra.sql-transaction never observes individually (only active transactions get one) — ActiveCount itself is reconstructable by counting those, so it isn't duplicated here.

infra.db-connection.note: One per open connection in TopOpenConnections (the full open-connection population, not capped — only its root-path enrichment is bounded). retained.bytes omitted when no dominator tree was available. An evidence entry with the formatted GC root-path as its Description is present only for the bounded root-path-enrichment subset that found a path.

infra.db-connection-type-population.note: One per distinct connection type — bounded by distinct type count, not per-instance. Backs the old finding generator's type-breakdown narrative (top-3 types by TotalCount across every state), which infra.db-connection (Open subset only) cannot.

infra.db-connection-population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Closed/Broken/Other/Unknown-state connections never get an infra.db-connection observation at all (only Open ones do) — OpenConnections/Gen2OpenConnections/Gen0OpenConnections are reconstructable by counting/filtering that stream instead, so they aren't duplicated here.

infra.http-object.note: One per instance sampled into TopHttpInstances (HttpClient/HttpWebRequest/ServicePoint/handler-tracking entries — the full population for these categories, never capped; HttpWebResponse/HttpMessageHandler are counted but never individually observed, see infra.http-object-population). generation.ordinal present only for HttpClient (0/1/2); connection-limit present only for ServicePoint when the field resolved.

infra.http-handler-module.note: One per distinct HttpMessageHandler-owning module — bounded by distinct module count, not per instance. Backs the old finding generator's 'largest contributor' module narrative, which HttpMessageHandler instances (never individually observed) cannot. Emitted in already-sorted-descending order.

infra.http-object-population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. HttpWebResponse and HttpMessageHandler instances are counted but never individually observed (no per-instance field extraction exists for either category), so their counts can't be reconstructed any other way.

infra.timer.note: One per distinct timer-shaped type name (bounded population). Interval histogram deliberately not emitted in this pass.

infra.wcf-channel.note: One per faulted channel — the same anomaly-relevant subset TopFaultedChannels already selects. retained.bytes omitted when no dominator tree was available. binding-hint.ordinal (WcfBindingHint) always present. An evidence entry with the remote endpoint address as its Description is present when one was read.

infra.wcf-channel-type-population.note: One per distinct channel type — bounded by distinct type count, not per-instance. Backs the old finding generator's faulted-type breakdown, which iterates types in TotalCount-descending order (not FaultedCount order), an order infra.wcf-channel's faulted-only stream can't reproduce on its own. Emitted in already-sorted-descending order.

infra.wcf-channel-population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Every count here except FaultedChannels covers channels/factories infra.wcf-channel's faulted-only stream never observes individually; FaultedChannels is reconstructable by counting that stream, so it isn't duplicated here. Also emitted (factory-only) when zero channels were found but factories exist — a real measurement, not a missing-capability condition.

runtime.jit-activity.note: Single whole-run observation. No per-method observation yet — building a real MethodRef needs name/signature splitting ThreadStackFrameRef doesn't expose structurally, so Phase 5 step 2 didn't attempt one either: top-method.hot-size-bytes/cold-size-bytes are TopLargestMethods[0]'s sizes, and an EvidenceRef carries its pre-formatted Signature string as free text (no identity resolution needed for evidence, unlike a Subject) — large-method.count is TopLargestMethods.Count (every method already over LargeMethodThresholdBytes), not a second, different count.

heap.segment-kind-composition.note: One per segment-kind row (bounded to 5: SOH/LOH/POH/Frozen/Unknown) — distinct taxonomy from MemoryAnalyzer's generation-labeled heap.segment-composition. fragmented.bytes (Phase 5 step 2) is present on the SOH/LOH/POH/Frozen rows only — HeapTopologyDomainResult carries no UnknownFragmentedBytes field (the Unknown-kind local accumulator is computed but never returned), so the Unknown row's measure would have to be fabricated, not read. TotalCommittedBytes/TotalSegments/SohBytes/SohSegmentCount/LohBytes/LohSegmentCount/PohBytes/PohSegmentCount/FrozenBytes/LohPercent/PohPercent all need no whole-run measures either: they're exact sums (or, for the two percentages, sum-then-divide using the same formula HeapTopologyAnalyzer.Analyze itself uses) over this observation's 5 rows.

heap.poh-type-composition.note: One per type in TopPohTypes (capped by HeapTopologyAnalyzerOptions.TopSegmentsCount).

heap.frozen-type-composition.note: One per type in TopFrozenTypes (capped by HeapTopologyAnalyzerOptions.TopSegmentsCount).

heap.topology-population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. logical-heap.max-bytes/min-bytes are the extremes across PerLogicalHeapSummaries, computed here rather than observed per-heap: the logical-heap-skew finding only ever reads the two extremes, never any individual heap's identity, and PerLogicalHeapSummaries itself has no natural EntityRef (a logical heap index, not a type/thread/object).

runtime.module-heap-footprint.note: One per module in TopModulesByHeapMemory — first real module-subject observation type.

runtime.module-population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. dynamic.count (DynamicModules, from the single global EnumerateModules() pass) is genuinely distinct from total-dynamic.count (TotalDynamicModules, summed across a separate per-AppDomain enumeration pass — the same physical dynamic module counted once per domain it's loaded into) despite the similar names.

runtime.module-conflict-group.note: One per ConflictDetails entry (bounded by distinct-module-with-a-version-conflict count, process-scale not heap-scale). Evidence[0].Description carries the comma-joined Versions list — no home among Measures for a string list.

runtime.module-type-density.note: One per HeavyTypeDensityModules entry, already sorted descending by bytes-per-type.bytes before emission — the rule trusts that order for the "worst" module, same already-sorted-before-emission structure ArraySynthesisRule relies on. A different, filtered population than runtime.module-heap-footprint (DensityAnomalyMaxTypes/MinBytes-gated, not top-by-total-bytes).

runtime.module-cross-domain-load.note: One per CrossDomainModuleLoads entry (bounded by MaxCrossDomainModulesToReport), already sorted before emission — the rule trusts that order.

runtime.module-assemblyref-mismatch.note: One per AssemblyRefVersionMismatches entry (bounded by MaxAssemblyRefMismatchesToReport). Subject identifies RequiringModule; Evidence[0].Description carries "{RequiredAssemblyName} {RequiredVersion} (loaded: {LoadedVersions})" — three string fields with no home among Measures, combined into the one free-text slot since the finding text always renders them together.

runtime.module-unknown-identity.note: One per UnknownIdentityDuplicateModules entry (a HashSet<string>, process-scale not heap-scale) — emitted in that set's own enumeration order, the same order the old finding generator's Take(5) read directly from the (unordered-by-contract, but stable-in-practice) set.

runtime.active-exception.note: One per exception instance whose address matches a thread's live current-exception — only the active subset, not the (potentially storm-scale) full scanned exception population.

runtime.crash-population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Always emitted, including the zero-exception case, since these are exhaustive scalars Analyze always computes.

runtime.crash-thread-candidate.note: One per distinct thread carrying an active exception (bounded by thread count, never heap-scale), already sorted descending by active-exception.count before emission — the rule trusts that order for the "primary exception type" of the top thread, the same already-sorted-before-emission structure ArraySynthesisRule relies on. Cannot be reconstructed from runtime.active-exception alone: that observation's Subject identifies only the exception type, not which thread it belongs to, so per-thread grouping needs its own observation.

type.shape-composition.note: Single whole-heap observation. Per-type Top*Types lists excluded — Category is a hand-picked-threshold classification over the entire type population (Smell A/B + volume risk).

type.boxing.note: One per boxed value type found on the heap — a small fraction of the whole type population, unlike ObjectShapeAnalyzer's lists.

type.array-composition.note: One per distinct array element-type+rank combination — exhaustive despite the 'Top' name, no cap. array.rank/loh.*/pinned.* added in 1.43.0 (Phase 5 step 2 audit finding) specifically so a synthesis rule can reconstruct LohArrayBytes/PinnedArrayBytes exactly by summing across all entries — gen2-plus-loh.percent alone can't, since it blends gen2 and LOH into one ratio.

heap.sparse-array.note: One per TopSparseArrays entry (bounded, sparse ratio >= 0.5).

heap.large-array.note: One per TopLargeArrays entry (bounded to whatever the LOH satellite index/fallback captured). Backs the finding generator's 'largest array element type' narrative — Phase 5 step 2 audit finding, this was previously unobserved.

heap.pinned-array.note: One per TopPinnedArrays entry (bounded, options.TopPinnedArrayLimit). Backs the finding generator's 'largest pinned array element type' narrative — Phase 5 step 2 audit finding, this was previously unobserved.

collection.wasteful.note: One per TopWastefulCollections entry — already-selected as capacity-mismatched, bounded by TopWastefulCollectionsToShow. retained.bytes omitted when no dominator tree was available.

heap.long-string.note: One per string at or above VeryLongStringThresholdBytes — a small fraction of the whole string population. TopDuplicates excluded (no stringValue entity kind in the SDK yet).

type.async-state-machine.note: One per distinct async-state-machine type — already narrowly scoped by IsCandidateType's regex, not the whole-heap type population. Subjects[1] added in 1.44.0 (Phase 5 step 2 audit finding): a Low-fidelity MethodRef (no real parameter signature available from a type name alone) carrying DeclaringType/OriginatingMethod, so a synthesis rule can group by method the same way SuspendedMethodMap already does, without duplicating the analyzer's own name-parsing regex.

type.async-captured-closure.note: One per async-state-machine type with captured closure bytes > 0.

type.orphaned-task.note: One per orphaned task (no continuation, not completed/canceled) — deliberately uncapped; a large count under a real leak is itself the honest signal.

async.task-population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject (whole-process scalars), the same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Covers the task/TCS/VTS health signals type.orphaned-task cannot: cycle detection, old-generation pending/unresolved counts, fault count, continuation-chain depth. Emitted even when total.count is 0, since TCS/VTS population is independent of the task scan.

heap.static-root.note: One per analyzed static root. This analyzer has a known, documented upstream bug (HeapRootKind.StaticVar never fires on ClrMD 4) deliberately left unfixed, so this code path is currently unreachable on real dumps — correct for when the fix lands, not exercised today.

static-root.population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Scoped to the *significant* subset (a config-threshold filter, IsSignificant) unlike heap.static-root's every-analyzed-root population, so root.count/retained.bytes can't be reconstructed by counting/summing that stream. Always emitted, including the zero-significant-roots case (also currently unreachable, same known bug as heap.static-root), since both scalars are exhaustively computed either way.

type.root-reachability.note: One per top-by-size type sampled — bounded to ReferenceChainOptions.TopCount. retained.bytes omitted when no dominator tree was available.

reference-chain.type-sample.note: One per TopTypeSampleTraces entry — a different, richer population than type.root-reachability (which is skipped when a type has no sample address, and predates the multi-sample enrichment pass this observation reads from). Evidence[0].Description carries the dominant root-kind string (e.g. "Finalizer"), which has no home among the fixed-count Measures — null/absent when no retained sample resolved a root kind. Backs the finalizer-only-retention finding.

reference-chain.population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Always emitted, including the no-samples case, since these are exhaustive scalars Analyze always computes. Backs the no-samples finding, the retention-coverage finding, and the traversal-limit finding.

reference-chain.shared-root-group.note: One per SharedRootGroups entry (already sorted descending by type count, then ascending by root address, before emission — the rule trusts that order the same way ArraySynthesisRule trusts pre-sorted lists). Subject is the shared root object's own address (an ObjectRef, the first per-analyzer observation to use it as the sole Subject rather than a TypeRef). Evidence[0].Description carries the root kind string, Evidence[1].Description the comma-joined type-name list — neither has a home among Measures or a single typed EntityRef.

type.retention.note: The canonical type.retention example from observation-and-correlation-model.md § 4. One per TopDominatorTypes entry; retained.bytes uses the exact Lengauer-Tarjan dominator-tree value when the §D9 overlay succeeded for that type, otherwise the heuristic BFS estimate (Confidence 0.7 in that case). estimated-retained.bytes (Phase 5 step 2) is always the heuristic BFS estimate, exact or not — the old finding generator's top-suspect finding reads TypeSnapshot.EstimatedRetainedBytes unconditionally, never the exact overlay value, so retained.bytes alone can't back it once the overlay succeeds.

type.retention-population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Backs the highly-referenced-objects and reference-tracking-capped findings, neither of which type.retention's per-type stream can provide.

type.retention-hotspot.note: One per TopRetentionTypes entry (aggregated from TopHighlyReferencedObjects by type, bounded by RetentionOptions.TopHighlyReferencedObjectsToShow). Backs the dominant-retained-type-hotspot finding, which picks the entry with the highest total-incoming-references.count — not necessarily the first emitted, since TopRetentionTypes is itself sorted by estimated-retained bytes, not incoming-reference count.

event.publisher-leak.note: One per publisher/event group in TopPublisherEvents — bounded to the top 50 by subscriber count.

event.publisher-leak-group.note: One per TopLeakGroups entry — the full, unbounded per-group population (unlike event.publisher-leak's top-50-by-subscriber-count sample from a different list, TopPublisherEvents), and the one the instance/static aggregate findings actually read. Evidence[0].Description carries EventFieldName, which has no home among Subjects' typed EntityRef kinds (Subject alone identifies only the publisher type).

event.publisher-leak-population.note: One whole-run observation per analysis — no entity subject, same pattern as gc.generation-composition. Always emitted, including the zero-leak case, since these are exhaustive scalars Analyze always computes. Backs the zero-leak-signature finding and the group-count fallback used when TopLeakGroups happens to contain no group of a given IsStatic value even though the real count is nonzero.
